stories.title: Stephen Curry Signs 1-Year, $62.6M Extension — Staying a Warrior
stories.angle: Curry signs 1-year $62.6M extension (over-38 rule limits deal to 1 year); first player to earn $60M+ in a single season; officially stays with the only franchise he's ever played for; extension window opened Aug 29 and was signed immediately

He'll be the FIRST player in NBA history to earn $60M+ in a single season.

Always. A. Warrior. #Warriors #NBA

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text:
Steph Curry joins LeBron, Paul George, and KD past $500M in career earnings.

facebook.long_form:
Window: 9:00 AM ET

IT'S OFFICIAL — STEPH CURRY IS STAYING A WARRIOR! 🏆

The Golden State Warriors and Stephen Curry have agreed to a 1-year, $62.6 million contract extension, keeping the greatest shooter in NBA history in Golden State through the 2026-27 season.

Here's what makes this deal truly historic: Curry will become the FIRST player in NBA history to earn more than $60 million in a single season. To put that in perspective — he'll surpass what some teams pay their entire roster.

The extension window opened yesterday (August 29), and Curry didn't waste a single day. His agent Jeff Austin of Octagon confirmed the deal to ESPN's Adrian Wojnarowski almost immediately.

Why the 1-year deal? The NBA's over-38 rule limits extensions for players who would turn 38 during a multi-year contract. Curry, currently 36, is bound by this restriction. But make no mistake — the Warriors are committed to their franchise icon for as long as he wants to play.

With this signing, Curry becomes just the 4th player in NBA history to surpass $500 million in career earnings, joining LeBron James, Paul George, and Kevin Durant in that elite financial tier.

Curry has never played for another franchise in his entire career. That loyalty works both ways — and Golden State just made sure of it.

What do you think — can the Warriors make a playoff push with Curry leading the way?

---

article.headline: Stephen Curry Signs 1-Year, $62.6M Extension — Staying a Warrior for One More Historic Season

facebook.long_form:
Window: 11:00 AM ET

THE KAWHI LEONARD TORONTO RETURN IS GETTING VERY REAL 🦖

According to NBA insider Jake Fischer of NBC Sports, Kawhi Leonard is "increasingly confident" that his trade from the LA Clippers to the Toronto Raptors will be finalized before training camp begins on September 28.

Quick recap of how we got here:
• End of June: Clippers and Raptors agree on trade (Kawhi to Toronto for Brandon Ingram + Gradey Dick + two unprotected first-round picks + pick swaps)
• The deal was put on hold while the NBA investigated potential salary cap violations by the Clippers
• Last week: The NBA cleared the Clippers of the Aspiration cap circumvention charge
• Now: The NBA Board of Governors is expected to meet in September to determine any remaining Clippers sanctions before officially greenlighting the trade

Kawhi and the Raptors are already operating as if the trade will happen — they're planning for his arrival at Quebec City training camp starting September 28.

Remember: Kawhi Leonard won Toronto its ONLY championship in 2019, then left for the Clippers immediately. Seven years later, he's coming home.

For the Raptors, this is a massive swing — they're getting a two-time Finals MVP and one of the best two-way players of his generation, even if Father Time is catching up.

Do you think this Kawhi reunion is what Toronto needs? ⬇️

---

stories.title: Wemby Leads France vs. Sweden Today in FIBA Qualifier

"I do not miss the NBA right now, I miss FIBA basketball." #FIBA #Spurs

facebook.long_form:
Window: 1:00 PM ET

CAPTAIN WEMBY IS IN FULL CONTROL 🇫🇷

Victor Wembanyama leads France against Sweden TODAY (3:30 PM UTC) in the FIBA Basketball World Cup Qualifier — and the French national team looks absolutely dominant heading into the matchup.

Here's where France stands:
• 6-1 record in Group L — best in the group
• Beat Slovenia 92-67 in their last game (Wemby: 22 pts, 9 reb, 60% from the field)
• Survived a thriller against Serbia 91-90 earlier this month (Wemby: 18 pts; Jokic had 34/13/5 in a losing effort)
• Wemby was named France captain for this qualifying window

Wembanyama himself said it best: "I do not miss the NBA right now, I miss FIBA basketball."

For context on what France has in Wemby: this is the guy who won the NBA Defensive Player of the Year award, earned All-NBA honors, led the San Antonio Spurs to the Western Conference Finals, and already signed a 5-year, $252 million extension. At just 22 years old.

Sweden is a capable opponent, but France — with Gobert, Fournier, and Wemby as the backbone — enters as a heavy favorite.

Are you watching? 👀

NBA TRAINING CAMP IS 30 DAYS AWAY — Here's Every Transaction You Need to Know 🏀

With camps opening September 29 (veterans report Sept 28), teams are putting the final pieces in place for the 2026-27 season. Here's your quick roundup of the latest moves:

🔄 JONATHAN KUMINGA — 2-year, $12.43M deal with the Minnesota Timberwolves (Aug 26). The young forward who came up through Golden State now joins Anthony Edwards and the newly arrived LaMelo Ball in Minnesota.

🔄 DEMAR DEROZAN — 1-year, $3.88M veteran minimum with the Denver Nuggets (Aug). DeRozan, who averaged 18.4 ppg with Sacramento last season, joins Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray in a revamped Denver lineup.

🔄 BENNEDICT MATHURIN — 2-year, $16M deal with the New Orleans Pelicans. Mathurin gets a fresh start in New Orleans.

🔄 NICK RICHARDS — 1-year, $3.06M with Miami Heat (Aug 27). Gives the Heat a backup center behind Bam Adebayo.

Key Dates to Circle:
• Sept 22 — Overseas players report (e.g., Toronto Raptors for Kawhi Leonard)
• Sept 28 — Veterans can report
• Sept 29 — Training camps officially open
• Oct 3 — Preseason begins
• Oct 20 — OPENING NIGHT (Knicks raise their first banner since 1973!)

Which team do you think is best set up heading into camp? ⬇️

South Beach hasn't looked this dangerous in years. #HeatNation #NBA

facebook.long_form:
Window: 7:00 PM ET

THE MIAMI HEAT HAVE BUILT SOMETHING SPECIAL 🔥

With the signing of big man Nick Richards this week, Miami's roster is essentially set heading into training camp — and it's one of the most intriguing lineups in the entire NBA.

Here's who the Heat are rolling with:

🌟 Giannis Antetokounmpo — Traded from Milwaukee on July 6 (Raptors sent Jimmy Butler + others to MIL for Giannis + Portis; Heat sent Herro/Ware/Jaquez/picks). Two-time MVP coming to South Beach.
🌟 Bam Adebayo — The anchor stays. Still one of the best two-way centers in basketball.
🌟 Klay Thompson — Signed 2-year, $11.48M deal after Dallas buyout. "I still have a lot to prove," he said at his Heat intro.
🌟 Nick Richards — 1-year, $3.06M deal. Gives them a physical presence as Bam's backup.
➕ J'Vonne Hadley + Keshad Johnson on two-way deals (Aug 28)

The Heat have a Christmas Day game against the Boston Celtics on December 25 — you can bet that matchup will be circled on every Heat fan's calendar.

Oh, and one more thing: Giannis becomes eligible for a $275 million supermax extension on January 6, 2027. The Heat's plan is simple — show him they can win, then lock him in long-term.

Are the Heat your pick to come out of the East?
